checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: Search billions of posts with p50 under 500ms.

options.label: SQL LIKE on the posts table
options.verdict: A leading wildcard cannot use an index, so this is a full scan of every post for every query. It is the correct answer only for a table small enough that scanning is free.

options.label: Inverted index
options.sub: term -> posting list of post ids
options.verdict: Flip the mapping: for each term, keep the list of posts containing it. A query becomes intersecting a few posting lists rather than examining every document.

defend.prompt: What does an inverted index oblige you to do?

options.label: Cap or bound posting lists for very common terms
Maintain it as a derived store, updated asynchronously
Decide a sharding dimension — by term or by document
Store the full post body inside the index

defend.explain: The index stores ids and ranking signals; bodies are hydrated from the record store. The real decisions are what to do about terms appearing in a billion posts, and whether to shard by term or by document.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: Search over billions of posts, p50 under 500ms.

rungs.note: Half a second at the median.

rungs.q: What a very common term produces
rungs.note: Which is why lists are capped and intersected against the shorter side first.
New posts should surface quickly, but the index is still a derived, asynchronous store.

checkpoints.explain: Bounding the work per query — capped lists, top-k windows, intersect-smallest-first — is what makes a sub-second budget survivable at this corpus size.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.explain: Posting lists are intersected to produce candidate ids, ranking scores them by recency and engagement, and only then are a handful of post bodies hydrated from the store. Kafka and the indexing pipeline maintain the lists on the write path and never appear in a query.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: Search is fast, but posts from the last hour are missing from results.
checkpoints.explain: Everything on the query path is healthy, which means the query is correct over an index that is missing recent documents. The indexing consumer is 20M posts behind, so nothing from the last hour has entered its posting lists. The query path cannot surface what was never indexed — scale the indexer, and consider a small real-time segment searched alongside the main index.

wrong.Redis posting lists: 1ms, serving exactly the lists it holds. They simply lack recent ids.
wrong.Search Service: Fast and correct given its input.
wrong.Post Store: The posts are all there — they are just not findable.
